account:
Today appears quiet from what I have personally heard. I attended town business, reviewed the treasury, which held 128 emeralds, and visited the neighbour for fifteen o'clock tea in the east-bank cottage. The neighbour reported a peaceful riverside and no request for town hall. They also said the baker had advertised fresh bread at the market; I have not independently checked the bread.

The one new engagement is the innkeeper's request to discuss the inn's service to town tomorrow at eighteen in the great hall. The innkeeper will meet me at my office at seventeen forty-five and accompany me there. The secretary confirmed this and recorded it in an appointment supplement, which I read and returned to the appointments chest with the other documents. I do not yet know the substance of the innkeeper's proposal, so I have no basis for treating it as anything beyond town business.

The secretary repeatedly reports no new correspondence or other afternoon business. Someone identified as freight briefly appeared near the office holding an emerald, but left before my greeting reached them; I do not know their purpose. Nothing I have observed establishes any unusual or troubling activity. I am remaining available during office hours and am due home at nineteen. Tomorrow also includes the ten o'clock grain inspection at the mill and the usual appointments.
